name: Abstracted hardiness
summary: A stand-in for the many loci that set a horse's hardiness. One allele raises it, one lowers it, and the two copies add. The real trait is polygenic; this single locus is an abstraction, not a claim about a real gene.

phenotypes.name: Wild type
phenotypes.description: Ordinary constitution for whatever the horse's own genes say - which, since most horses carry a copy of this one, is itself slightly unusual.

phenotypes.name: Frailer
phenotypes.description: One frail copy. The same thing in reverse: less hardy by the percentage on that copy, usually around a tenth, and inherited with the allele.

phenotypes.name: Much frailer
phenotypes.description: Two frail copies, and the percentages subtract together. Around a fifth under on average and a great deal less at the extreme - though never all the way to nothing.

phenotypes.name: Hardier
phenotypes.description: One hardy copy. Hardier than the horse's own genes would make it, by the percentage written on that copy - usually around a tenth. It passes that exact percentage on with the allele.

phenotypes.name: Balanced
phenotypes.description: One hardy copy and one frail copy. Their percentages very nearly cancel, so the horse keeps close to its ordinary hardiness while carrying, and passing on, both extremes.

phenotypes.name: Much hardier
phenotypes.description: Two hardy copies, and the percentages add. Around a fifth over on average, and far more when both copies are strong ones - the toughest horses in the world are bred here, because no wild horse is born with two.
